description: B1 practice sets for the grammar topics that had none, written by hand (2026-10-13). Imported and published.

lessons.title: Have You Ever… or Did You…? Present Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.description: Practise choosing between the Present Perfect and the Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: I ___ that series last weekend.
exercises.explanation: A finished time (last weekend) needs the Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: ___ you ever ___ sushi?
exercises.explanation: Experience at any time in your life: Have you ever + past participle.

exercises.prompt: She ___ in London since 2020.
exercises.explanation: since + a starting point and the action continues now: Present Perfect.

exercises.prompt: We ___ (meet) at a concert two years ago.
exercises.explanation: ago shows a finished time, so the Past Simple: met.

exercises.prompt: I ___ (not finish) my homework yet.
exercises.explanation: yet in negatives goes with the Present Perfect.

exercises.prompt: “I have seen him yesterday” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: yesterday is a finished time, so: I saw him yesterday.

exercises.prompt: “She has just posted a new video” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: just + Present Perfect for something that happened a moment ago.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.
exercises.explanation: already, ever, since go with the Present Perfect; last summer (a finished time) with the Past Simple.
Have + you + ever + been: a question about experience.

exercises.prompt: When ___ you start learning English?
exercises.explanation: Questions with When ask about a finished time: Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: I ___ to Paris three times. I love it there!
exercises.explanation: Experience up to now (how many times): Present Perfect.

lessons.title: I Was Doing… When: Past Continuous
lessons.description: Practise the Past Continuous for actions in progress and its use with the Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: At 8 pm yesterday I ___ dinner.
exercises.explanation: An action in progress at a moment in the past: was cooking.

exercises.prompt: They ___ football when it started to rain.
exercises.explanation: they + were + -ing for the longer action.

exercises.prompt: I ___ (watch) TV when my phone rang.
exercises.explanation: The longer action in progress: Past Continuous.

exercises.prompt: While she was walking home, she ___ (see) an old friend.
exercises.explanation: The short action that interrupts: Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: “We was talking when the teacher came in” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: With we we use were: We were talking.

exercises.prompt: “What were you doing at midnight?” is a correct question.
exercises.explanation: Question: was/were + subject + -ing.
Long action (was sleeping) + when + short action (went off).

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.
exercises.explanation: Past Continuous gives the background; Past Simple gives the event.

exercises.prompt: What ___ you doing when I called you?
exercises.explanation: you + were in the Past Continuous.

exercises.prompt: The sun ___ (shine) and the birds were singing. It was a perfect morning.
exercises.explanation: Describing the scene in a story: Past Continuous.

lessons.title: I Used To…: Past Habits
lessons.description: Practise used to for past habits and states that are not true now.

exercises.prompt: I ___ play the piano when I was a child.
exercises.explanation: Positive past habit: used to + base verb.

exercises.prompt: She ___ like vegetables, but now she loves them.
exercises.explanation: After didn't we write use to (without d).

exercises.prompt: ___ you use to watch cartoons every morning?
exercises.explanation: Question: Did + subject + use to.

exercises.prompt: My dad ___ to have long hair. Now he is bald!
exercises.explanation: A past state that is not true now: used to.

exercises.prompt: “I used to go to the gym tomorrow” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: used to is only about the past, not the future.

exercises.prompt: “We used to live in a small village” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: A past state: used to live.
There used to be = there was in the past but not now.

exercises.prompt: Match the past and the present.

pairs.I used to be shy,: but now I love talking to people.
pairs.He used to hate maths,: but now it's his favourite subject.
pairs.We used to live in a flat,: but now we have a house.

exercises.explanation: used to describes something that was true before and isn't now.

exercises.prompt: Did they ___ to go camping every summer?
exercises.explanation: In questions with did: use to (no d).

exercises.prompt: When I was ten, I ___ to bed at 9 pm every night.
exercises.explanation: A repeated action in the past: used to go.

lessons.title: If I Were You…: Second Conditional
lessons.description: Practise the second conditional for imaginary situations and advice.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ a million dollars, I would travel the world.
exercises.explanation: Second conditional: If + Past Simple, would + base verb.

exercises.prompt: If she lived closer, she ___ visit us more often.
exercises.explanation: The result part uses would + base verb.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ you, I would talk to her.
exercises.explanation: For advice we say If I were you.

exercises.prompt: If we ___ (know) the answer, we would tell you.
exercises.explanation: If + Past Simple: knew.

exercises.prompt: What would you do if you ___ (meet) your favourite singer?
exercises.explanation: Imaginary situation: if + Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: “If I would have more time, I would learn Japanese” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: No would after if: If I had more time…

exercises.prompt: “I wouldn't do that if I were you” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: The if part can come second: no comma needed then.
Result (would + verb) first, then if + Past Simple — no comma needed.

exercises.prompt: Match the halves.

pairs.If it weren't raining,: we would go to the beach.
pairs.If I had a dog,: I would walk it every day.

exercises.explanation: Each imaginary condition matches its logical result.

exercises.prompt: What ___ you do if you lost your phone?
exercises.explanation: Imaginary question: What would you do if…

lessons.title: It Was Made In…: The Passive
lessons.description: Practise the passive in the present and past: is made, was built.

exercises.prompt: English ___ in many countries.
exercises.explanation: Present passive: is + past participle.

exercises.prompt: This bridge ___ in 1890.
exercises.explanation: Past passive with a finished time: was + past participle.

exercises.prompt: These phones ___ (make) in China.
exercises.explanation: Plural subject, present passive: are made.

exercises.prompt: The window ___ (break) by a football yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Past passive: was + broken.

exercises.prompt: “The cake was ate by my brother” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: We need the past participle: was eaten.

exercises.prompt: “The song was written by a 16-year-old girl” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: was + written (past participle) + by + who did it.
Subject + were + past participle + by + agent.

exercises.prompt: Match the active sentence with the passive one.

The room is cleaned every day.

exercises.explanation: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.

exercises.prompt: When ___ the first iPhone released?
exercises.explanation: Past passive question: When was … released?

exercises.prompt: The emails ___ (not send) yesterday because the internet was down.
exercises.explanation: Negative past passive, plural: weren't sent.

lessons.title: Who, Which, That: Relative Clauses
lessons.description: Practise who, which, that and where to add information about people, things and places.

exercises.prompt: She is the girl ___ won the competition.
exercises.explanation: For people we use who (or that).

exercises.prompt: This is the phone ___ I bought last week.
exercises.explanation: For things we use which (or that).

exercises.prompt: That's the café ___ we first met.
exercises.explanation: For places, where = in which.

exercises.prompt: I have a friend ___ speaks four languages. (who / which)
exercises.explanation: A person, so who (that is also possible).

exercises.prompt: The film ___ we watched yesterday was scary. (who / which)
exercises.explanation: A thing, so which (that is also possible).

exercises.prompt: “The boy which lives next door is my best friend” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: For people we use who or that, not which.

exercises.prompt: “The book that you gave me is amazing” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: that can be used for things.
noun + who + verb.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.
exercises.explanation: who → people, which → things, where → places.

exercises.prompt: Do you know the man ___ car is parked outside?
exercises.explanation: whose shows possession: the man's car.

lessons.title: Doing or To Do? Gerund and Infinitive
lessons.description: Practise verbs followed by the -ing form or by to + verb.

exercises.prompt: I enjoy ___ to music while I study.
exercises.explanation: enjoy + -ing.

exercises.prompt: She decided ___ a new language.
exercises.explanation: decide + to + verb.

exercises.prompt: We want ___ a film tonight.
exercises.explanation: want + to + verb.

exercises.prompt: He finished ___ (write) his essay at midnight.
exercises.explanation: finish + -ing.

exercises.prompt: They hope ___ (visit) Japan next year.
exercises.explanation: hope + to + verb.

exercises.prompt: “I avoid to eat sugar” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: avoid + -ing: I avoid eating sugar.

exercises.prompt: “Swimming is good for your health” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: The -ing form can be the subject of a sentence.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.
exercises.explanation: enjoy and mind + -ing; promise and plan + to + verb.
After a preposition (at) we use -ing.

exercises.prompt: Would you mind ___ the window?
exercises.explanation: mind + -ing.

lessons.title: You Should…: Giving Advice
lessons.description: Practise should, shouldn't and ought to for advice and opinions.

exercises.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.
exercises.explanation: Advice: should + base verb.

exercises.prompt: You ___ eat so much junk food. It's bad for you.
exercises.explanation: Negative advice: shouldn't.

exercises.prompt: We ___ to leave now, or we'll miss the train.
exercises.explanation: ought to = should.

exercises.prompt: ___ I tell her the truth? What do you think? (Should / Ought)
exercises.explanation: Questions asking for advice: Should I…?

exercises.prompt: “He should to study more” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: No to after should: He should study more.

exercises.prompt: “You ought to apologise” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: ought to + base verb.
shouldn't + base verb.

exercises.prompt: Match the problem with the advice.

You should drink some water and rest.
You should write it in your planner.
You should try a new hobby.

exercises.explanation: should + verb gives a suggestion that fits the problem.

exercises.prompt: It's very cold. You ___ wear a coat. (should / shouldn't)
exercises.explanation: Good advice in cold weather: should.

exercises.prompt: What do you think I ___ do?
exercises.explanation: What do you think I should do? — asking for advice.
